body:
Independent reproduction of **Bug 2**, plus five controls that narrow down what it is *not*. Setup matches yours closely: private GitHub marketplace declared via project `extraKnownMarketplaces`, plugin installed at **project scope** in five repositories, `"autoUpdate": true` on the marketplace entry.

Claude Code 2.1.228, Windows (win32 10.0.26100).

### Observed

The marketplace registry entry's `lastUpdated` advances during a session, but `installed_plugins.json` records never move. Publishing a new plugin version and moving the tracked ref changes nothing for existing installs; only an explicit `claude plugin update <plugin>@<marketplace> --scope project`, run once per project directory, moves them.

### Controls

1. **Not a headless artifact.** First measured with `claude -p`; re-measured in a normal interactive session left open **13.8 min** (past the documented ≤10 min delay). Same result.
2. **Not cross-session interference.** Closed every session, opened exactly one. Registry `lastUpdated` advanced during it, so the refresh ran and was not throttled — installs still did not move.
3. **`autoUpdate` is honored.** It is present as `"autoUpdate": true` in `known_marketplaces.json`, so the project-level setting does reach the registry.
4. **Not authentication.** A credential helper is configured; `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 git ls-remote <repo> <ref>` returns without prompting, and a manual `git fetch` inside the marketplace clone succeeds and advances the remote-tracking ref.
5. **Not scope.** I also installed the same plugin at **user** scope and left a 13-minute session open in an unrelated directory. The user-scope record did not auto-update either, so this is not specific to per-project installs.

### Working control case on the same machine

This is the part that I think localizes it. In a **single** auto-update pass (timestamps within the same second):

| | official marketplace | our marketplace |
|---|---|---|
| structure | **not a git clone** (no `HEAD`, no fetch refspec) | git clone |
| registration | seed/managed | settings-sourced (`extraKnownMarketplaces`) |
| `ref` | none | pinned |
| installs updated | **yes** (2 plugins, user scope) | **no** (5 installs, project scope) |

Both registry entries were stamped in that pass; only the official marketplace's plugins actually moved. Since control 5 rules out scope, the asymmetry appears to follow the marketplace *type* / refresh path rather than the install scope.

Related: the source-side never refreshed either — the clone's `refs/remotes/origin/<ref>` did not move while `lastUpdated` was being stamped. That matches the cache-only path described in #83777.

### Bug 1 — also reproduced

Independently hit the same silent absence: `enabledPlugins` + `extraKnownMarketplaces` committed to a repo's `.claude/settings.json`, no install record for that project path, and sessions ran with none of the plugin's rules, skills or hooks — no warning. On two separate machines. Worth adding: starting a session does **not** register a settings-sourced marketplace either; an explicit `claude plugin marketplace add` was required, so the "commit two files and you're done" pattern silently does nothing on its own.

Our mitigation for Bug 1 is a **plugin-independent** `SessionStart` hook committed in each repo (deliberately not in the plugin — a plugin cannot report its own absence). It checks whether the plugin cache directory exists and prints install instructions if not.

### On "no lag signal"

We added one on our side, in case it is useful as a suggestion: our plugin's own `SessionStart` hook reads the installed `plugin.json` version, reads the version from the marketplace catalog copy on disk, and when the catalog is ahead it writes a `stale=<installed>-<catalog>` field to a local log and warns in-session. It is entirely local (no network, one file read) and stays silent when the versions agree. Something equivalent surfaced natively would have saved us roughly a day: every symptom of this bug is invisible, and the version field in a log was the only channel that ever reported it.
